what: tempo's build census said `LEFT 79 lower: Lowered` and `LEFT 20 lower: Convert` with one example each, so the causes under them could not be counted. The first one shown (tokio `select!`'s `$crate::select_priv_clean_pattern`) was refused by the host as `Host(HostError { ask: ProcMacro, why: Refused })`, which looked like a missing proc-macro path in bodies. In fact the survey's program was built with no body sources at all (`Store::sources` was None), so every body proc-macro call, `env!` and `include!` was refused before any runner was asked. `blaze build`'s lazy program already set them.
cost: about an hour reading the host, the hook and the resolvers before finding that the census tool alone lacked the sources
cause: the census's program had a constructor that left out an input the real command passes, and the class cut the Debug form at its first `{`, so one variant hid every cause
whys: make_from had no body-sources parameter (the lazy program set them after construction); class_of kept only the outer variant name
class: a measurement tool that builds the thing under test differently from the command, and a census class too coarse to count causes
prevention: done: make_from takes body_sources, and every caller passes it (None only for given-file programs with no package); body_failed classes `Lowered` by the first finding's typed cause chain (BodyFinding::Macro has `cause`) and `Convert` by the refusal and the type builder's why; test front2_body_proc_macro (with sources the runner is asked; control without sources leaves the fn out, class names ProcMacro)
